newsitem.title: USA: Rep. Kennedy's popularity continues to fall - poll.
newsitem.headline: Rep. Kennedy's popularity continues to fall - poll.

text.p: Democrat Representative Joseph Kennedy's popularity with Massachusetts voters continues to sink under the weight of his brother's sex scandal and his own marriage annulment controversy, according to a poll in Thursday's Boston Globe.

Kennedy, who as of Wednesday said he intends to run for governor, remains a strong candidate in the Democratic gubernatorial primary, but has fallen well behind each of the likely Republican nominees, Lt. Gov. Paul Cellucci and state Treasurer Joseph Malone, the survey for the Globe and WBZ-TV survey found.
Massachusetts governor William Weld would handily beat Kennedy if the election were held today, the poll showed. However Weld has said he will not run for a third term.

The telephone poll of 400 likely voters conducted Tuesday and Wednesday found 34 percent view him favourably, while 45 percent rate him unfavourably. A similar poll taken in late April had Kennedy with a 43 to 39 percent favourable rating, the newspaper said.
As recently as January, Kennedy was viewed favourably by 60 percent of those asked.
All three surveys had a five-point margin of error.

"The poll shows continuing erosion in Kennedy's popularity," Gerry Chervinsky, president of KRC Communications Research, which conducted the poll, told the newspaper. "We see no evidence that it has bottomed out."

A local prosecutor suspended the investigation into allegations that Kennedy's brother, Michael, had sex with his family's teenage babysitter and said on Tuesday charges will not be filed because the alleged victim refused to cooperate.
Kennedy's first wife Sheila Rauch Kennedy has been on a national tour promoting her new book "Shattered Faith" detailing how the congressman bullied her into a divorce and annulment.
The congressman publicly apologised several times to his wife and the babysitter's family.
